program.name: Additional targeted overdose-prevention outreach and naloxone distribution

scope.counterfactual: Existing SF public naloxone supply and other distributors continue; the gift funds additional outreach doses.

utility.label: Health utility of survivors
utility.rationale: Downward transfer from 0.799 for HIV-negative daily heroin injection, allowing comorbidity and population differences.

sources.publisher: Patton et al., Quality of Life Research
sources.title: Analyzing quality of life among people with opioid use disorder from the NIDA Data Share initiative

annualHazard.label: Annual all-cause mortality hazard after a nonfatal overdose
annualHazard.rationale: Central informed by 778.3 deaths per 10,000 person-years in a US overdose-survivor cohort. Note: a higher hazard lowers QALYs, so p90 here is the pessimistic case.

sources.title: Causes of Death After Nonfatal Opioid Overdose

sources.publisher: Weiner et al., Annals of Emergency Medicine
sources.title: One-Year Mortality of Patients After Emergency Department Treatment for Nonfatal Opioid Overdose

horizonYears.label: Credited survival horizon
horizonYears.rationale: Truncates benefits because recipient ages and long-term outcomes are unknown; not a life expectancy.

costPerDose.label: Donor cost per additional dose delivered
costPerDose.rationale: About 2x the $9.61 planned bundle/target-dose benchmark, rounded, allowing extra outreach effort and delivery shortfalls. Not an SFAF quote.

sources.title: Proposed SFAF agreement 1000032060
sources.locator: $250,000 annual budget, 26,016 target doses = $9.61 per target dose

marginalYieldRetention.label: Share of reported reversal yield retained at the margin
marginalYieldRetention.rationale: Aggregate judgment for harder-to-reach expansion, displacement, reporting mismatch and repeat recipients in a heavily supplied SF market.

additionalSurvivalPerReversal.label: Additional acute survivals per retained reversal
additionalSurvivalPerReversal.rationale: Credits one additional acute survivor per 50 retained reported reversals; spontaneous survival and alternative rescue are common in SF.

reportedReversals.label: Reversals reported by the organization in the reference year

sources.title: Overdose prevention and response; 2025 service reporting

reportedDoses.label: Doses distributed by the organization in the same year

sources.title: Overdose prevention and response; 2025 service reporting

costPerOutcome.unit: USD per additional opioid-overdose deaths averted

qalysPerNativeOutcome.unit: QALYs per additional opioid-overdose deaths averted

qalyLayer.notes: probabilityNonPositive is 0 by construction: v1 input distributions are strictly positive, so the null case lives only in nullBoundary.

simulation.notes: Inputs drawn independently. Legacy SF scenarios were joint corners; independent draws give a narrower price spread than those corners.

fundingRoom.nextEvidence: Current additional outreach plan, executed costs, unmet coverage and recipient-linked rescue records.

nullBoundary: If the gift replaces existing provision or reaches no otherwise-fatal events, deaths averted are zero and there is no finite price.

sessions.evidence: Legacy model data/san-francisco/sfaf-naloxone-cea-v1.json; interval not recorded in data/research-effort.json. Factoring into this template: open-botec design session 2026-10-18.
